correctness.rationale: For L>0 and a nonantipodal pair the normalized arguments of L+i(h±t) belong to the same right-half-plane branch. The determinant of the old and new double-angle vectors has sign given by 2t[(L−K)+(1−L)t²], and for t>0 both arguments lie strictly between 0 and pi; hence the determinant gives the actual direction of motion. The separation update is odd and increasing, and all monotone bounded orbits must approach finite fixed points. The determinant lists exactly the finite separators and settles K=L as repelling at zero for 0<L<1. The antipodal pairs are fixed and the identity is exactly the L=1,h=0 boundary. The diagonal multiplier L/K and the antipodal half-angle multiplier L give geometric convergence in the applicable cases. The midpoint defects are even and O(t²) near consensus after subtraction of the rigid increment, and O(t^−2) near antipodality, so they are summable. At L=1,h≠0, expanding the positive-t antipodal distance gives epsilon^+=1/t+(h²−1/3)/t³+O(t^−5), so t^+²=t²−2h²+O(t^−2). Uniform upper/lower bounds on the square decrement above any sufficiently large cutoff, and bounded subsequent residence in any fixed compact positive interval before hitting T, prove the escape constant. The proof's final epsilon_0 t_0 should read epsilon_0 |t_0| for both signs; by oddness the stated squared limit is correct. The midpoint angle is taken modulo 2pi and is defined off exact antipodality, where the full state instead remains fixed. Independent direct complex iteration, without executing the uploaded checker, corroborated the regime directions and the limiting escape scale (for h=±0.8, normalized times 0.78809, 0.78320, 0.78186 at |t_0|=32,64,128, versus 0.78125).
